# Haira

> The programming language for AI agents and workflows.

Haira is a compiled, general-purpose programming language designed for building agentic AI applications. It compiles to Go, then to a native binary — zero dependencies, zero boilerplate.

## Core Concepts

Haira has four agentic keywords built into the language:

- **provider** — LLM backend configuration (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible API)
- **tool** — Functions with LLM-visible descriptions, type-checked with compiler-enforced documentation
- **agent** — LLM entity with a provider, system prompt, tools, memory, and optional handoffs
- **workflow** — Function with an HTTP trigger (`@post`, `@get`, etc.) that exposes agents as API endpoints

## Key Features

- Compiles to a single native binary via Go codegen
- Generative UI: agents render rich components (tables, charts, forms, status cards) via `ui.*` helpers
- ARP (Agentic Rendering Protocol): transport-agnostic protocol for agent-to-renderer communication
- Auto-generated web UI for every workflow (forms for regular, chat UI for streaming)
- SSE streaming with `-> stream` return type
- Agent handoffs: agents delegate to specialized agents automatically
- Agent memory: `conversation(max_turns: N)` per session
- MCP support: consume external tools and expose workflows as MCP tools
- Parallel execution via `spawn { }` blocks
- Pipe operator: `data |> transform |> output`
- Pattern matching with or-patterns, range patterns, and guards
- 10+ stdlib packages: postgres, sqlite, excel, vector, slack, github, gitlab, langfuse

## Language Syntax

Haira uses familiar C-style syntax with Go-inspired simplicity:

```haira
import "http"

provider openai {
    api_key: env("OPENAI_API_KEY")
    model: "gpt-4o"
}

tool get_weather(city: string) -> string {
    """Get the current weather for a city."""
    resp, err = http.get("https://wttr.in/${city}?format=j1")
    if err != nil { return "Failed." }
    return resp.body
}

agent Assistant {
    provider: openai
    system: "You are a helpful assistant."
    tools: [get_weather]
    memory: conversation(max_turns: 10)
}

@post("/chat")
workflow Chat(message: string) -> stream {
    return Assistant.stream(message)
}

fn main() {
    http.Server([Chat]).listen(8080)
}
```
